newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine group sells Russia 29,200 T/yr beef.
newsitem.headline: Argentine group sells Russia 29,200 T/yr beef.

text.p: An Argentine group has signed a contract to export 29,200 tonnes of beef a year to a private Russia buyer through the year 2000, a firm spokesman said Tuesday.

Argentine packers Col Car and Frigorifico Novara, both from Cordoba province, will send the beef for processing to a private Russian firm which supplies the Russian army in the Saint Petersburg area, Col Car advisor Ricardo Schiavoni said.
"The value of the operation is over $50 million, over the full duration of the contract," Schiavoni told Reuters.
It will be the first time the packers sell beef to Russia, which earlier this year approved imports from Argentina due to its elimination of foot-and-mouth disease from its 50-million head herd.

In June, the United States government granted final authorization for a 20,000-tonne quota of Argentine fresh beef imports, shortly after the International Epizootic Office in Paris declared Argentina foot-and-mouth free.
Argentina is now aggressively seeking access to world beef markets, and exported about 500,000 tonnes in 1995 and 1996.
Col Car and Novara already exports to Africa, Hong Kong and to Argentina's partners in South America's Mercosur customs union.
